newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-COLE GOAL LEAVES MANCHESTER UNITED TOP OF PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLE GOAL LEAVES MANCHESTER UNITED TOP OF PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Manchester United triumphed in the second part of their Wimbledon trilogy on Wednesday, beating the London side 2-1 to go top of the premier league for the first time this season.

United, who drew 1-1 with Wimbledon in the fourth round of the F.A. Cup on Saturday and face them again in the replay next Tuesday, dominated the match and hit the crossbar three times with stunning long-range strikes.
But they fell behind on the hour when Chris Perry poked home an Alan Kimble corner.
Welsh forward Ryan Giggs equalised for the champions after 76 minutes with an artful front-post header from a David Beckham corner.
United, playing in front of a premier league record crowd of 55,314, surged forward, sensing victory against a Wimbledon side which had been unusually subdued from the outset.

With seven minutes to play Beckham crossed from the right, man-of-the-match Ole Gunnar Solskjaer hit a sweet volley which goalkeeper Neil Sullivan managed to block, and striker Andy Cole, who had come on as a second-half substitute, nipped in to fire home the winner.
Victory takes United to 47 points from 24 matches, one ahead of Liverpool, who were not playing, and Arsenal, 2-1 winners at West Ham.
Newcastle remain fourth after a remarkable comeback at home to out-of-form Everton, whose disgruntled manager Joe Royle dropped goalkeeper Neville Southall for the first time since 1982.
The tactic appeared to have worked when Everton took the lead through Gary Speed after three minutes and then kept Newcastle at bay for over an hour.

But Newcastle struck four times in the last 16 minutes through Les Ferdinand (74), Robert Lee (79), Alan Shearer (penalty 83) and Robbie Elliott (90), to give manager Kenny Dalglish his first league victory since he took over from Kevin Keegan earlier this month.

Arsenal's victory came courtesy of Ray Parlour and the league's top scorer Ian Wright, who latched on to a Paul Merson pass after 67 minutes to beat Ludek Miklosko for his 17th league goal of the season.

Defeat means West Ham remain in the relegation zone with just one win from their last 16 matches. Their only consolation was that a threatened pitch invasion by disheartened fans failed to materialise.
One place ahead of West Ham are Nottingham Forest, who witnessed the return of a much loved figure at the City Ground.
Brian Clough, who managed the club for 18 years from 1975 and guided them to two European Cups in the late 1970s, made his first appearance at a first-team home match since he quit in 1993.
Clough was given a standing ovation as he made his way to his seat to watch his son Nigel in action on the pitch and responded by blowing kisses to the crowd.
The party atmosphere soon evaporated though. Forest lost 1-0 to fellow strugglers Coventry.

On an evening of comebacks, second division Stockport came from a goal down to triumph 2-1 at premier league Southampton in a League Cup quarter-final replay. Substitute Andy Mutch scored their winner in the 83rd minute.
Stockport face premier league Middlesbrough in the semifinal and are within sight of a first Wembley appearance in a major cup final.
